transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Northbound CTO), Ben Ramirez (Lead ML Eng), Claire Zhou (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto): Weekly ops windup, focused on reliability signals and finops; pilot scoping next week.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for making time, uh happy Wednesday. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Asha: Asha here.
[00:06] Ben: Ben -- good to go.
[00:07] Claire: Claire, yep.
[00:09] Priya: Priya from Redwood, hi.
[00:10] Jordan: Great. Goal for today is twofold — one, review your uptime and burn trends from last quarter, and two, lock down the bench and pilot ask. Also surface any blockers for Private/VPC route.

[03:15] Jordan: We pulled the last 30 days and I know you saw the dashboard but quick highlights: 99.7% uptime overall, with a couple of 5–8 minute tail incidents — mostly in the 02:00–03:00 UTC window which maps to your nightly batch.
[03:40] Ben: Right uh that window is when our enrichment job spikes token counts, yeah. We saw increased latency during KV cache misses.
[03:50] Priya: (overlap) Yep, the KV cache behavior here is expected — once the prefix isn't in memory the cold starts add 80–120 ms on our infra. We recommended a small persistent warm pool in the ded- pool to cut that.
[04:12] Ben: Sorry ded pool?
[04:14] Priya: I meant dedicated pool — sorry, my mic cut. Dedicated capacity with a small always-on slice reduces those misses. There's a tradeoff vs cost obviously.

[06:00] Asha: Speaking of cost — we actually hit a burn spike after last month's promo. It doubled token spend for a 48-hour window. We need better guardrails so marketing doesn't blow the runway.
[06:12] Jordan: Understood. We can set per-route hard caps and soft throttles; also offer suggested batching configs. For this workload your cost per 1k tokens drops by about 18% with 4x batching assuming latency SLO can accept 50–80ms increase on tail.
[06:33] Claire: Is that batching during online requests? Our UX team is very latency sensitive on customer-facing flows.
[06:38] Priya: Right. For the chat flows we don't recommend aggressive batching. For async enrichment we can batch more aggressively. There's also prefix caching — keeping hot prefixes reduces per-token compute.

[08:20] Ben: On model side what quantization profile were you recommending? We tried 8-bit q4 but saw hallucination increase in some long-context prompts.
[08:29] Priya: We flagged Q4-8 as higher risk for your long context. For production we suggested mixed approach: 4-bit for embeddings-heavy paths, 8-bit for short-turn chat, and keep fp16 or int8 on the core customer support flow. In short: don't do a full account-level quantize, do route-level profiles.

[11:00] Asha: Security checklist — we need SOC 2 evidence, a KMS flow and SAML for SSO. Also audit logs for token-level tracing. What can you share today?
[11:12] Jordan: We have SOC 2 Type II artifacts and our security pack; Priya will attach the KMS integration guide and SAML playbook after the call. Audit logs are available in the Console for last 90 days — we can extend retention as an add-on.
[11:35] Claire: For Private deployment — network wise how tight is the peering? We run strict egress rules.
[11:40] Priya: We support VPC peering and peering over private link. There's a small control-plane handshake that uses TLS on 443; we can provide IP ranges and a maintenance window. Also HSM/KMS can be customer-managed in on-prem packages.

[14:50] Ben: For the bench — what inputs do you need from us to run a 24-hour cost/latency run?
[14:56] Jordan: Great Q. Ideally a sample traffic trace (JSON lines of requests) with time-of-day distribution, sample prompt set, target SLOs, and any must-preserve behaviors (no dropped tokens, strict order). If you can share a 2-hour compressed sample that represents peak and a longer 24-hour synthetic replay, we can run it in staging.
[15:25] Ben: I can get that. We'll scrub PII and send via the secure share.

[18:00] (small cross talk)
[18:12] Priya: One more operational note: smart routing policies can fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency is noncritical — we can configure weightings and auto-failover. That helps cost during promos.
[18:32] Asha: But how deterministic is behavior across models? We can't have customer-visible quality regressions.
[18:38] Priya: We do a model diff on eval sets — Redwood Optimize recommends compatible model variants with pass/fail thresholds for your eval prompt set. We'll surface regression alerts. For sensitive flows we recommend pinning versions.

[22:10] Claire: We're also worried about incident response — can Redwood integrate into our PagerDuty?
[22:16] Jordan: Yes PagerDuty and Splunk hooks are available; we can push alerts for SLO breaches and error rates. We'll also share the playbook for our on-call escalation.

[25:50] Ben: On the reserved capacity pricing — can you run a scenario: 3x baseline with burst to 5x during peak? We want to see commit vs on-demand math.
[26:01] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll model monthly committed and burst allowances. For your numbers the committed baseline with 3x should save ~28% vs pure on-demand; the exact depends on token mix and sequence lengths. I'll include a burn projection table.

[29:35] Asha: Any regards to data residency? Some customers in EU require data not leaving region.
[29:42] Priya: We have region pinning and private deployments in EU regions. For on-prem we support air-gapped options as well.

[33:00] (quiet for 20s while someone types)
[33:18] Ben: Quick technical nit — the KV cache TTL we saw set to 5 minutes. Would bumping to 30m impact memory footprint significantly?
[33:26] Priya: It will increase memory but you get far fewer cache misses; the runtime can also evict by LRU. We can recommend a sweet spot based on your token distribution — typically 15–30m works for enrichment workloads.

[37:40] Jordan: Ok time for decisions — three asks for the week: 1) Ben to share traffic sample and prompt set, 2) Priya will publish SOC2/KMS/SAML docs, 3) Jordan will send pilot pricing + reserved capacity scenarios. Anyone pushback?
[37:55] Asha: No pushback, timeline is tight though — Finance wants pilot numbers by Monday.
[38:02] Jordan: We'll aim for Monday. 

[41:10] Claire: On the bench run — will it be in your hosted test cluster or our Dedicated staging?
[41:17] Priya: For fidelity we prefer staging on Dedicated mirror where possible — otherwise hosted sim with traffic replay but Dedicated mirror gives you realistic caching and KV effects. If you can approve a short Dedicated mirror window, that's the path.

[44:40] Ben: Let's try the Dedicated mirror for the 24-hour run. I'll get Claire to approve the peering window.
[44:48] Claire: Yep I'll confirm maintenance windows after lunch tomorrow.

[47:05] Jordan: Cool — recap of next steps (brief): Jordan send pricing, Priya attach security kit and integration notes, Ben provide traffic sample, Claire confirm VPC window. We'll run bench week of 11/23 and share results with a short readout.

[47:30] Asha: One last thing — can you include an example of the rollback behavior if a new model rollout regresses in quality? We need clear canary/rollback docs.
[47:40] Priya: Yes, we have canary policies and automatic fallback to previous pinned model; we'll include the runbook.

[50:00] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[50:05] Asha: Thanks all.
[50:07] Ben: Thanks.
[50:08] Claire: Bye.

End notes: Action items above. Shared links to be sent: pricing spreadsheet, SOC2 pack, KMS + SAML guide, bench script and replay instructions.
